key_insight: Frontier models performed unevenly on expert-authored clinical reasoning tasks, with much lower success on the most critical rubric items than on low-stakes details.
clinical_relevance: For clinical decision support, this suggests models may appear competent while still missing the highest-priority reasoning steps that matter most to patient safety.
method: Five clinician-authored scenarios across anaesthesia, internal/family medicine, emergency medicine, and obstetrics
Each scenario used an atomic weighted rubric with 25-62 criteria, totaling 184 criteria
Three frontier models were scored against expert golden answers using rubric-based evaluation
evidence_signal: Mean rubric pass rates were 0.47 for Claude Opus 4.7, 0.39 for GPT 5.4, and 0.37 for Gemini 3.1 Pro, while critical weight-5 criteria passed only 32.4-41.7% of the time and 52% of critical items were missed by all models.
watch_item: This is a small preliminary dataset, so results are useful for benchmarking methods but not yet enough to generalize to broad clinical use.
paper_title: A rubric-based controlled comparison of frontier language models on expert-authored clinical reasoning tasks
